chunks: And whatever is narrated from Al-Nuʿman ibn Saʿd, the companion of Amir Al-Muʾminin, peace be upon him, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Al-Husayn Al-Saʿdaʾbadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah Al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Thabit ibn Abi Ṣafiyyah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Al-Nuʿman ibn Saʿd.

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir Al-Muʾminin (Commander of the Faithful), referring to Imam Ali
key_terms.السَّعْدَآبَادِي: Al-Saʿdaʾbadi, a nisba indicating origin or residence
key_terms.النُّعْمَانِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ: Al-Nuʿman ibn Saʿd, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.الْبَرْقِيُّ: Al-Barqi, a nisba indicating origin or family name
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature

ai.seo_question: Who is the chain of narrators for the hadith of Al-Nuʿman ibn Saʿd in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage serves as a detailed isnad verification for a report from Al-Nuʿman ibn Saʿd, highlighting the scholarly rigor of Shaykh al-Saduq in tracing the lineage through key figures like Al-Barqi and Ibn Sinan. It underscores the importance of reliable transmission chains in Shia hadith sciences, ensuring the authenticity of teachings attributed to the Ahl al-Bayt. The mention of specific narrators reflects the historical context of hadith compilation during the early Islamic period.
